html:
The largest outbreak of Ebola virus disease on record, which spread through Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone from December 2013 to June 2016.

Earlier outbreaks, since the virus was identified in 1976, had hit remote villages in Central Africa and died out within months. This one began in a village in southeastern Guinea, probably with a small child infected by an animal, and reached the crowded capitals: Conakry, Monrovia and Freetown. All three countries had weak health systems, still worn down by years of civil war.

Ebola spreads through the body fluids of the sick and the dead, so nurses, doctors and families who washed bodies for burial were hit hard. In August 2014 the World Health Organization declared an international emergency, and foreign help poured in. Cases peaked that October. By the end, 28,616 people had been infected and 11,310 had died, and the true toll was likely higher. Smaller outbreaks reached Nigeria and Mali, and a few cases reached the United States and Europe. Trials during the epidemic led to the first Ebola vaccine, approved in 2019.
sum: The largest outbreak of Ebola virus disease on record, which spread through Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone from December 2013 to June 2016.
